record.context_brief: Fixed points on non-fibered symplectic manifold
record.original_question: Let (M^{2n},ω) be a compact symplectic manifold with Euler characteristic χ(M^{2n}) = 0 that does not fiber over S^1. Does every symplectic diffeomorphism of (M^{2n},ω) that is homotopic to the identity have at least one fixed point, and in fact at least as many fixed points as the minimal number of zeros of any symplectic vector field on M^{2n}?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $(M^{2n}, \omega)$ be a closed (compact, without boundary) symplectic manifold of dimension $2n$ whose Euler characteristic satisfies $\chi(M^{2n}) = 0$, and assume that $M^{2n}$ does not fiber smoothly over the circle $S^1$. A symplectic vector field on $(M^{2n}, \omega)$ is a smooth vector field $X$ whose flow preserves $\omega$, equivalently $\mathcal{L}_X \omega = 0$. Let $N(M, \omega)$ denote the minimum, taken over all symplectic vector fields $X$ on $(M^{2n}, \omega)$, of the number of zeros of $X$.

Prove or disprove: every symplectic diffeomorphism $\varphi : M^{2n} \to M^{2n}$ that is smoothly homotopic to the identity has at least one fixed point, and in fact has at least $N(M, \omega)$ fixed points.
artifact.status_search_result: A web search did not surface a resolution of this specific Arnold-type conjecture for symplectic (not necessarily Hamiltonian) diffeomorphisms on closed symplectic manifolds with vanishing Euler characteristic that do not fiber over $S^1$. The standard Arnold conjecture concerns Hamiltonian diffeomorphisms, and this stronger statement for symplectic diffeomorphisms homotopic to the identity, with the lower bound given by the minimal number of zeros of symplectic vector fields, appears to remain open.

status_evidence.title: Symplectomorphism - Wikipedia
status_evidence.snippet: Arnold conjectured that any symplectic diffeomorphism of a compact symplectic manifold, homologous to the identity, has as many fixed-points as a function on the manifold has critical points.
status_evidence.claim: Arnold's conjecture concerns fixed points of symplectic diffeomorphisms; the standard form is about Hamiltonian (homologous to identity) diffeomorphisms, with no general resolution in the broader symplectic-isotopic case discussed here.

status_evidence.title: On Arnold's conjecture for symplectic fixed points
status_evidence.snippet: Discusses Arnold's conjecture for symplectic fixed points and its known partial cases.
status_evidence.claim: Known results concern restricted classes (Hamiltonian, specific manifolds); the conjecture for symplectic diffeomorphisms merely homotopic to identity on non-fibered $\chi=0$ manifolds is not reported as resolved.
